title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the 'équation des lacets' programme, solving [α,ρ]=ξ in GL(M) or SL(M) over a base. The previous page shows that the solutions form a torsor under the centraliser T_ρ, the unit group scheme of A_ρ. Zariski-local triviality of such torsors reduces the obstruction to an invertible A_ρ-module. The obstruction in SL comes from the norm map to G_m.

This page specialises to ρ = [[0,1],[-1,1]] in SL2(Z) over A = Z.
- The characteristic polynomial of ρ is x²−x+1. So A_ρ = Z[ρ] ≅ Z[ζ6], the Eisenstein integers, i.e. the ring of integers of Q(√−3) = Q(primitive cube root of −1).
- ρ acts as multiplication by e^{iπ/3} = (1+i√3)/2. ρ has order 6 and is, up to conjugacy, ST in SL2(Z).
- Write ξ = [[A,B],[C,D]]. Then ξρ = [[−B, A+B],[−D, C+D]]; this is computed correctly.
- The necessary conditions b), c) of the 'proposition' are det ξ = 1 and Tr(ξρ) = Tr ρ. They say that ξρ = αρα^{-1} has the same characteristic polynomial as ρ. They become (16): AD−BC = 1 and C+D−B = 1. Grothendieck calls these 'bien familières'.
- His claim: under (16), one can locally find α ∈ ΓGL(2) with αρα^{-1}ρ^{-1} = ξ. Indeed ξρ with characteristic polynomial x²−x+1 makes M an A_ρ-module; when it is locally cyclic, this module is invertible. The obstruction to global conjugacy to ρ is the class of the invertible A_ρ-module Hom_{A_ρ}(A_ρ, M) in Pic(A_ρ).
- Over Z, Pic(Z[ζ6]) = 1 (class number one), so a global solution in GL2(Z) exists. This is the Latimer–MacDuffee correspondence in scheme-theoretic dress.
- The next page continues: det α ∈ {±1} is independent of the choice of α, because units of A_ρ have norm f·f̄ = +1. So solvability in SL2(Z) is governed by a sign. He conjectures the sign is D mod 3.
- That conjecture is consistent with the abelianisation SL2(Z) → Z/12. A commutator lies in the kernel. If det α = −1, then αρα^{-1} lies in the SL2(Z)-class of ρ^{-1}, and ξ maps to an element of order 3, detected through SL2(Z) → SL2(F3) → Z/3.
errors: The claim 'sur une base quelconque' (local conjugacy of ξρ to ρ given only det and trace) fails without a regularity hypothesis at the prime 3, where x²−x+1 ≡ (x+1)². Over F3, ξ = −ρ^{-1} satisfies AD−BC = 1 and C+D−B = 1, yet ξρ = −I is scalar and not conjugate to ρ. One needs ξρ to be locally cyclic (non-scalar mod 3); over Z this is automatic.
Minor: 'Q(∛−1)' is ambiguous notation; what is meant is Q(√−3) = Q(ζ6), ζ6 being a non-real cube root of −1. The identification is otherwise correct.

ideas.what: Integer matrices with fixed characteristic polynomial x²−x+1 are classified up to GL2(Z)-conjugacy by Pic of Z[ζ6], which is trivial.
Solving the commutator equation [α,ρ]=ξ as a torsor under the centraliser torus T_ρ = unit group scheme of A_ρ, with obstruction an invertible A_ρ-module, i.e. a class in Pic(A_ρ).
ideas.modern_name: Torsor/Picard obstruction for conjugacy of regular elements (Weil restriction tori as centralisers)

ideas.what: Reduction of the condition for ξ to be a commutator with ρ (order 6) to the equations AD−BC=1, C+D−B=1, plus a sign obstruction for SL2(Z) (next page, conjecturally D mod 3).
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (two SL2(Z)-classes of elements of order 6; abelianisation known since the 19th–early 20th century)

missed.claim: This is a scheme-theoretic treatment of commutator equations [α,ρ]=ξ in GL2/SL2 over arbitrary bases. It links the 'équation des lacets' (relations in the Teichmüller/GT setting) to class groups of the order Z[ρ]. Mathematically it is classical; it documents how Grothendieck approached the loop equations via arithmetic of quadratic orders.
missed.quote: l'obstruction est A_ρ-module inversible, or A_ρ principal sauf erreur, i.e. (17) Pic(A_ρ) = 1
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of mainly historical interest for reconstructing the 'Longue Marche' programme; no new result.

deep.surprise_reason: Correct but classical computation: Eisenstein integers, Latimer–MacDuffee and class number one. There is a small gap at the prime 3 for arbitrary bases. The interest is purely in documenting the method within the loop-equation programme.
transcription_corrections: 'loc. sur une α ∈ ΓGL(2)' should read 'loc. Zar. une α ∈ ΓGl(2)' (locally for the Zariski topology).
'A_ρ^* [-est-] principal' is better read as 'A_ρ est principal sauf erreur'. The 'est' is struck and rewritten, and the asterisk-like mark is a footnote or insertion sign, not the unit group.
The label '(15)' before ξ = (A B; C D) is struck through in the manuscript.
The diagonal marginal note is largely illegible; it seems to mention the possibility of (W-)interpretation of ξρ and a 'relation … fibre'.
